title: Colorful Cosmic Reflections
caption: The reflection nebula NGC 2170, imaged by the SMARTS 0.9-meter Telescope
credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA Image Processing: Travis Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage), M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab) , & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Bright swathes of color streak across this image of the reflection nebula NGC 2170. Dust grains bounce back blue light from hot stars buried inside the nebula, warm hydrogen gas glows deep red, and dark tendrils of dust absorb the light of stars and gas behind them.

In a reflection nebula, diffuse clouds of interstellar dust scatter the light of nearby stars toward us. Blue light is scattered more readily than red, which is one reason reflection nebulae often look blue. In NGC 2170 that blue mixes with the red glow of hydrogen and the dark threads of dust, so three different effects share one scene.

NGC 2170 belongs to Monoceros, the Unicorn, a dim constellation that straddles the celestial equator. The observations were made with the SMARTS 0.9-meter Telescope, which operates at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in Chile.

understand.summary: Taken with the Tek2K camera on the SMARTS 0.9-meter Telescope through g, r, i and hydrogen-alpha filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Long exposures gather far more light than the eye, so the nebula's colors appear far stronger than they would through a telescope.
